primitives.name: Spot Targeting Precision
primitives.verbatim_quote: An out-fielder should bear in mind one cardinal principle, namely, that he should run as fast as possible until he nears the spot MAKING SURE OF A CATCH.—LEFT-FIELDER CATCHING, CENTER-FIELDER BACKING HIM UP.
primitives.assumptions: Ball trajectory is predictable; fielder has accurate spatial estimation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High error when x_target ≠ x_ball due to misjudgment.

layer2.mapping: GSE spatial targeting algorithm mirrors GSI probabilistic landing prediction.
layer2.telemetry: Distance between predicted and actual catch location.

primitives.name: Moderate Runner Advantage
primitives.verbatim_quote: A moderate runner who starts instantly for the right spot makes a far better fielder than a more speedy man who gets off slowly, and whose judgment of the spot where the ball will probably land is not so good.
primitives.assumptions: Instantaneous reaction improves performance over raw speed alone.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t_reaction increases beyond threshold, performance degrades.

layer2.mapping: GSE decision-making kernel prioritizes reaction over speed; GSI evaluates trade-off via temporal efficiency.
layer2.telemetry: Reaction time vs. catch success rate ratio.
